title: Cold rebuild: A TTL cache
summary: Rebuild A TTL cache from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A TTL cache** in *Resolution and TTL*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A resolver cached a record at t=0 with TTL 300. Which requests are answered from cache?
steps.explain: At exactly TTL seconds the entry is expired; the resolver must go back to the authoritative server.

steps.title: Rebuild A TTL cache cold
prompt: - `void Put(string name, string value, int ttl, int now)` stores an answer received at time `now` (seconds).
- `string? Get(string name, int now)` returns the value if `now < storedAt + ttl`, otherwise removes it and returns `null`.
Names are case-insensitive. A new `Put` replaces the old entry.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
